skill.name: cookoff
skill.description: Coordinates a design-to-implementation cookoff where multiple agents create independent plans, implement in worktrees, compare results, and select a winner.
skill.summary: Run parallel implementation cookoffs from a shared design and select the strongest result.
skill.author: 2389-research

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and fenced examples, not Ruby shell execution. No prompt injection, network reconnaissance, or system reconnaissance evidence was found. The main risk is the cleanup workflow, which can delete worktrees and branches without explicit confirmation.

remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation and show a dry-run list before removing worktrees or deleting branches. Preserve loser branches unless the user approves deletion.

remediation.issue: Templated shell paths and branch names
remediation.suggestion: Validate and quote feature names before using them in filesystem or git commands. Avoid passing raw user text into shell commands.
State that companion skills should be installed from trusted sources and reviewed before use in the cookoff workflow.

static_findings.snippet: - `cookoff` - Same design, multiple cooks compete (each creates own plan + implements)
| `writing-plans` | `superpowers:writing-plans` | Each agent writes their own implementation plan |
| `executing-plans` | `superpowers:executing-plans` | Execute plan tasks sequentially with verificat
| `parallel-agents` | `superpowers:dispatching-parallel-agents` | Dispatch multiple Task tools in si
| `verification` | `superpowers:verification-before-completion` | Run command, read output, THEN cla
| `fresh-eyes` | `fresh-eyes-review:skills` (2389) | 2-5 min review for security, logic, edge cases
| `judge` | `test-kitchen:judge` | Scoring framework with checklists (MUST invoke at Phase 4) |
Use `parallel-agents` pattern. Send ONE message with multiple Task tool calls:
| `writing-plans` | 3 | Each subagent creates their own implementation plan |
| `parallel-agents` | 3 | Dispatch ALL subagents in SINGLE message |
| `verification` | 3, 5 | Before claiming done; before declaring winner |
| `judge` | 4 | **INVOKE** for scoring framework (loads fresh, ensures format compliance) |
Reason: Clean fresh-eyes review, solid data-layer-first architecture

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Cleanup Commands Need Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The cleanup workflow tells the agent to remove loser worktrees and force-delete branches. This can cause local data loss if branch names or worktree paths are wrong.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands shown in the cleanup block directly remove worktrees and delete branches with force. The risk is contextual data loss, not hidden malware.

content.value_statement: Complex features often have several valid implementation paths. This skill runs independent agent implementations, reviews them, and helps select the strongest result.
actual_capabilities: Offers implementation choices when a design is ready to build.
Assesses feature complexity and recommends two to five implementations.
Defines plan folders and worktrees for independent agent attempts.
Coordinates parallel agents that plan, implement, test, and report results.
Guides judging with tests, review findings, scorecards, and winner selection.
Records results and cleanup steps after a winner is chosen.
limitations: Requires a design document or clear shared implementation target.
Depends on companion skills when they are available.
Uses more time and compute than a single implementation path.
Cleanup commands need review because they can remove local branches.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Competing Feature Builds
use_cases.description: Run several independent implementations of a feature and compare quality before choosing one.

use_cases.title: Reduce Design Bias
use_cases.description: Let agents create separate plans from the same design instead of sharing one implementation plan.

use_cases.title: Document Build Decisions
use_cases.description: Capture plans, test results, review notes, and winner rationale for later team review.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Simple Cookoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt after a design is approved.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use cookoff for this approved design. Recommend the number of implementations and show the options before starting.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Three Implementations
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for a medium feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a three-agent cookoff from the design document. Each agent should write its own plan, implement, test, and report results.

prompt_templates.title: Judge With Review Signals
prompt_templates.prompt: Judge the cookoff results using tests, fresh review findings, design adherence, and maintainability. Explain the winner and rejected options.

prompt_templates.title: Manage Full Cookoff Lifecycle
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for end-to-end workflow control.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the full cookoff lifecycle. Create worktrees, coordinate agents, compare outputs, request approval before cleanup, and write the result summary.

output_examples.input: Use cookoff for the approved authentication design.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends three implementations because the feature touches authentication, data flow, and tests. It presents options before dispatching agents.

output_examples.input: Pick the winner from these cookoff results.
output_examples.output: The skill compares test status, review findings, design adherence, and maintainability. It recommends the strongest implementation with a short rationale.

output_examples.input: Finish the cookoff and clean up safely.
output_examples.output: The skill verifies the winning implementation, records the result summary, lists branches for cleanup, and asks before destructive deletion.

best_practices: Start from a stable design document so every agent has the same target.
Ask agents to create independent plans before writing implementation code.
Review tests, design adherence, and maintainability before selecting a winner.
anti_patterns: Do not give every agent the same detailed implementation plan.
Do not dispatch agents one at a time when the goal is parallel comparison.
Do not delete worktrees or branches before reviewing the cleanup list.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it after design approval, when you want several independent implementation options before choosing one.

faq.question: Does it write the design document?
faq.answer: No. It expects a design document or a clear design agreement before implementation starts.

faq.question: How many agents does it use?
faq.answer: It recommends two to five implementations based on feature complexity and risk.

faq.question: Does it require git worktrees?
faq.answer: The workflow is built around separate worktrees so each implementation stays isolated.

faq.question: Can it work without companion skills?
faq.answer: Yes, but companion skills provide stronger planning, execution, review, and finishing workflows.

faq.question: What should I verify before cleanup?
faq.answer: Check the winning branch, loser branches, worktree paths, and user approval before deleting anything.
